name: Cucumber juice skin tonic

lead: Cucumber juice skin tonic is a traditional home skin-care preparation: fresh cucumber is juiced and the liquid is dabbed on the face as a toner. Users like it for its cooling feel and its association with soothing, refreshed-looking skin.

Cucumber is about 95 percent water, which underlies the hydrating, refreshing reputation. Cucumber also appears in commercial cosmetics; a 2007 Chinese patent describes a cucumber juice face mask for dry skin. No clinical trial of a homemade cucumber juice tonic has been published.

paras: People typically blend or press fresh cucumber, strain the juice and apply it with a cotton pad or spray as a toner, sometimes mixed with other ingredients such as rose water. It is used in the same place in a routine as a toner, and results are the immediate cooling and freshness it gives. Fresh juice is kept chilled and used soon.

Topical cucumber is generally regarded as mild, but any fresh plant preparation can irritate or provoke an allergic reaction in some people, and homemade juice spoils quickly. People with skin conditions or allergies often patch test and consult a dermatologist.

chain: Water-rich juice applied as a toner
angle.text: Users apply chilled cucumber juice to the face for an immediate cooling, refreshing effect, which they associate with less puffy, more hydrated looking skin.

lead: Cucumber juice skin tonic, also called cucumber face tonic, is a traditional cooling preparation made from the juice of the cucumber and applied to the face. It is used as a toner for a hydrated, refreshed look.

Cucumber fruit is about 95 percent water and contains small amounts of vitamin C and polyphenols, with higher polyphenol levels in unpeeled fruit [1]. Those properties are the usual basis for its use as a refreshing, hydrating wash for the skin.

A 2007 Chinese patent describes a cucumber juice facial mask made from polyvinyl alcohol, carboxymethyl cellulose and sorbitol, stated to suit dry skin [2]. No human trial of cucumber juice used as a tonic has been published.

paras: The tonic is simply cucumber juice used as a skin toner. The fruit is about 95 percent water and provides about 2.8 mg of vitamin C per 100 g, a low amount, with polyphenols concentrated more in unpeeled fruit [1].

Cucumber remedies are attributed to Pliny the Elder, though that attribution is marked as needing a citation on Wikipedia [1]. In the 1600s, writer John Evelyn viewed cucumber as little better than poison when eaten [1].
A 2007 Chinese patent describes a cucumber juice face mask made from polyvinyl alcohol, carboxymethyl cellulose and sorbitol, suited to dry skin [2].
